newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge probes suspected accomplice of Jackal.
newsitem.headline: French judge probes suspected accomplice of Jackal.

text.p: France's top anti-terrorism judge launched a probe on Thursday into a German suspected of being the accomplice of notorious guerrilla Carlos the Jackal in a 1982 bombing, hours after she was extradited from Italy.
French investigators believe Christa-Margot Froehlich, 54, may be the key to jailing Carlos for life.

Justice sources said Judge Jean-Louis Bruguiere told Froehlich she was suspected of involvement in the Paris bombing, which killed a pregnant woman and injured 63 people. Froehlich was extradited to Paris from Rome earlier on Thursday.

Bruguiere is leading several probes into bombings and attacks blamed on the Venezuelan-born Carlos, whose real name is Ilich Ramirez Sanchez, and who has been in a French jail since August 1994 after he was captured in Sudan.
Justice sources said Froehlich was suspected of being an accomplice to murder and to destroying property with explosives. She was ordered held pending the investigation.
Arrested when she visited her jailed husband in Rome in October 1995, Froehlich refused to answer Bruguiere's questions on the April 22, 1982 attack, the sources said.
Froehlich is suspected of driving a car from former Yugoslavia which was packed with 20 kg (44 lbs) of explosives and blown up.

The target of the attack was the Arabic-language weekly newspaper Al Watan Al Arabi, known for its critical stance towards left-wing Arab governments. But it is also thought to have been aimed at forcing the release from French jail of two other Carlos accomplices.
Files from the former East German and Hungarian secret services also link Froehlich to the bombing of the Paris-Toulouse express train in March 1982, which killed five people.
Lawyers for Carlos, seized by French counter-intelligence in Sudan two years ago, have insisted he was not in France at the time of the bombing.
Sources close to the probe said Bruguiere believed the woman could be vital in linking Carlos, under investigation for six attacks from 1974 to 1983, to the blast.

Justice sources said that Froehlich's husband had struggled to resist the French extradition request for his wife. She had herself asked Italian authorities before travelling to Rome from Germany whether she would be arrested if she made the trip.
Italian authorities told her lawyers there was nothing pending against her in Italy but then arrested her in Rome at France's request, the sources said.
